persona.bio: Rosa, 38, runs her own wedding planning business with about twenty weddings a year. Everything runs through Gmail: couples, venues, florists, photographers, caterers. She answers inquiry emails, writes the same welcome and contract emails again and again, chases vendors and couples who haven't replied, and keeps budgets, timelines and guest lists in Google Sheets. She uses ChatGPT every day and pays for it. She has saved instructions about herself in it but never connected it to Gmail.

steps.title: Your inquiry replies, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your common replies are saved on your phone, each a few letters away. You type a short shortcut, tap the reply, and change only the name or the date. Inquiries come in many times a day, so the same answers stop being copied from old messages and are ready where you already type.

steps.title: Your client emails, saved once as Gmail templates
steps.read: Your common emails are saved in Gmail as templates, ready to fill in. You pick the template, fill the gaps, read it through, and send. Client emails come up many times a day, so each one starts from your own wording instead of an old email you have to clean up.

material.label: Your client emails
items:
Subject: Your wedding inquiry

Hi [first name],

Thank you so much for reaching out about your wedding on [date]. I’d love to learn more about what you have in mind. Could you send me your rough guest count, your budget range and your venue ideas, if you have any? Then I can put together options for you.

Warmly,
[my name]

Subject: Next steps for your wedding

Hi [first name],

It was great talking with you on [day]. Here is what we agreed on: [short summary]. Next I will [my next step] by [date]. Please [their next step] by [date]. Let me know if anything looks off.

Best,
[my name]

Subject: Your proposal is ready

Hi [first name],

I’ve attached your proposal for [date and venue]. It covers [what is included]. Take your time looking it over and send me any questions. I’m happy to talk it through on a call, just tell me a time that works.

Best,
[my name]

Subject: Checking in on [topic]

Hi [first name],

I wanted to follow up on my note from [day] about [topic]. I need [what I need] by [date] so we can keep everything on track. If something has changed, just let me know and we’ll adjust.

Thank you,
[my name]

Subject: Timeline for [date]

Hi [first name],

Attached is the draft timeline for your day. Please look at [key times] and tell me what you’d like to change. Once you approve it, I will share it with your vendors.

Best,
[my name]

safeUse: Never type a couple’s full names, phone numbers, home addresses or email addresses into ChatGPT. Use brackets instead.
Keep contracts, payment details and card or bank information out of it.
Leave out guest lists and any private family or health details a client shared with you.
Read every reply and email before it goes out, and check dates, prices and vendor details against your own calendar and contracts.
Fill in names, dates and venues yourself, after the draft is written.

design.today: You answer these many times a day, often by copying an old reply and checking the calendar first. You also look up the person's details before you answer.
design.newWay: Your most common replies are saved once, so a first answer to a new inquiry is a few letters away on your phone. You still check the calendar and look up their details, then fill the date and the person's name into the saved reply. Every reply is read by you before it goes out, and it keeps the same warm voice every time instead of depending on which old message you found.

steps.goal: Pick your ten most common inquiry replies, such as date open, date taken, and asking for guest count and budget.
Save instructions about you and your business so every reply sounds like you.
Make a project for inquiry replies and put your ten replies and tone notes inside it.
Save the ten replies so each one is a few letters away in text and chat.
Keep checking the date yourself before you pick which saved reply to use.
